heading: Doctrine as a weight vector, and temperature as the mechanism for being baited
body:
Lori, 2026-09-04, after a walk through the Maxis lineage: "Temperature is a good mechanism. As is a vector for actions." BANKED, NOT BUILT. Nothing in Nav.Tactics changes on the strength of this entry.

THE MECHANISM, from The Sims (2000). An agent contains no plan. Each OBJECT advertises what needs it can satisfy and by how much -- a fridge advertises hunger, a bed advertises energy -- and the sim weights each advertisement by how badly it wants that thing right now, then picks. The intelligence lives in the world; the agent holds a max() loop. Wright called it smart terrain. Its practical payoff is that an expansion pack's new object needed no AI change: every existing sim already knew what to do with it.

WHAT LORI TOOK FROM IT, in their words, two things.

  A VECTOR FOR ACTIONS. Doctrines stop being different CODE and become different WEIGHTINGS over the same advertisements. GuardDoctrine and PatrolDoctrine would share one scan and differ by a row in a table. The property that makes this worth having is not elegance, it is that a weight vector can be SWEPT and MEASURED -- see [[measure-before-deciding]] -- where a decision tree can only be read. A pad advertises repair, a chokepoint advertises cover, a wounded squadmate advertises support.

  TEMPERATURE. Richard Evans, AI lead on The Sims 3, chose actions with a Boltzmann distribution over the utilities, with a TEMPERATURE that is low when the sim is happy and HIGH when it is doing badly -- so a desperate agent is measurably more likely to take a low-utility action. Stress makes you erratic, expressed as one number.

WHY TEMPERATURE IS THE INTERESTING ONE HERE, and this is the whole reason it was banked rather than noted and dropped. This project exists for "guards that never retreat to repair and patrols that get baited". A PERFECT UTILITY MAXIMISER CANNOT BE BAITED -- that is what makes it a maximiser. So the exploitable imperfection is not a defect to be tolerated in a doctrine engine, it is the product. The Sims literature says it should be a KNOB rather than an accident of a decision tree's branch ordering, and Maxis broke their own optimiser three separate ways on purpose:
  - The sim does not pick the best. It picks at random from among the TOP SCORERS, because argmax "felt robotic and overly predictable" and a sim that meets its needs perfectly leaves the player nothing to do.
  - Evans' temperature, above.
  - The urinal rule: realistic bathroom spacing was implemented and then CUT, because correct behaviour was dull and random choice produced memorable moments.
A squad whose decision quality degrades under pressure is both plausible and precisely the thing a player learns to induce. That is the closest thing to a mechanism for "baitable" that has turned up.

THE CRITICISM, which is the half that will bite, and it is the same charge as SimLife. Utility systems are ILLEGIBLE as they grow: the structure that makes them extensible is the structure that makes "why did it do that" unanswerable, and behaviour trees' rigid transitions are called out as both their weakness and their strength for exactly this reason. Three more, all reported by practitioners rather than theorised: OSCILLATION between two near-equal scores re-evaluated every tick, whose standard fix is inertia, which is another tuning parameter; BREAKDOWN AT FINE GRANULARITY, where it works for goal selection and falls apart used for every action because there are too many values to hold in your head; and GLOBAL TUNING, because every advertisement competes in one scalar space, so adding a candidate silently re-weights everything already in it.
FOR THIS PROJECT THAT IS AN ARGUMENT FOR THE VIEWER, not against the mechanism. A weighting is exactly the kind of thing the inspector can show -- every candidate, its advertisement, its weighted score, and which one won -- and that is the difference between SimLife and SimAnt, where the pheromone trails were DRAWN and people actually learned something.

RED ALERT IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE, not the model, and I had this wrong first. I described its target selection as an advertisement scan; the actual code is 1996 C++ with a deep per-type class hierarchy, and any scoring is buried in overrides. Lori, having opened it: "Just briefly looking at the code I see it has tons of individual functions just for aircraft... I didn't even get out of the As." The aircraft sprawl is honest rather than sloppy -- aircraft do not pathfind through cells at all, and need landing, ammo and return-to-base, none of which fits the ground abstraction -- but the lesson stands: RA put the STATS in data (rules.ini, which is why the modding scene existed) and left the BEHAVIOUR in a class per unit type. The Sims put the behaviour in the data too. Same era, opposite call, and Lori's data-over-code position is the Sims one. See [[data-over-code]].
A WARNING THAT FOLLOWS FROM IT: MovementSystem is a grid, the same as RA's. If air ever arrives here it will not fit, and it will grow its own everything for the same honest reason.

CLEAN ROOM. The C&C and Red Alert sources are public since 2020/2025 under GPL v3 at github.com/electronicarts/CnC_Red_Alert. Reading is fine; identifiers, constants and transcribed structure must never reach this repo, and with GPL that is a licensing question rather than only hygiene. Nothing in this entry is transcribed -- the RA characterisation above is from general knowledge and from Lori's own glance, and it is recorded here as a NEGATIVE example. See [[clean-room-no-competitor-source]].

SOURCES, all public commentary rather than source: Mark Brown, "The Genius AI Behind The Sims" (gmtk.substack.com); Wikipedia "Utility system" and "Richard Evans (AI researcher)"; Dave Mark's Infinite Axis Utility System (gameai.com/iaus.php), the modern descendant; and practitioner write-ups on oscillation and granularity. Searched 2026-09-04: there is NO commentary on Red Alert's AI specifically -- the source-release coverage is entirely preservation and modding.

NOT DECIDED, and deliberately left open: whether any of this displaces SquadDoctrine's current shape, what a squad's "need" even is, and whether temperature belongs to a squad or to an agent. Lori called the mechanisms good; that is not a build order.

heading: Morale is health plus the guns beside you, minus the guns hitting you
body:
Lori, 2026-09-04, working the morale model out loud across one conversation. BANKED, NOT BUILT. Nothing in Nav.Tactics changes on the strength of this entry, and the forks left open at the end are open on purpose.

THE MODEL, in Lori's words assembled in order.

  "morale includes health" -- health is not an alternative trigger to morale, it is an INPUT to it. Total War morale takes casualties alongside fatigue, flanking and whether the unit beside you just broke. Nobody triggers retreat on health ALONE; the interesting part is what else gets in.

  "We can have morale increased by the total amount of damage per second in local range - this will make all higher ranks dying or retreating more expensive."

  "part of your base is your health, and you get the bonus for your dps potential"

  "it's their actual dps, not their potential unless it's 'surprise, you're dead' level" -- and the worked case: "here's an auto-cannon that deals 50dps, and I have a max of 12".

SO THE SHAPE IS: morale = your own health (the base) + friendly DPS POTENTIAL in local range (the bonus) - enemy ACTUAL DPS on you, except that an enemy whose POTENTIAL can kill you inside one exchange counts at full potential whether or not it is firing.

WHY THE FRIENDLY/ENEMY ASYMMETRY IS NOT A BALANCE TWEAK. It is what the formula collapses to when a side is only allowed to use what it knows. You know your own side's guns because they are yours, so friendly POTENTIAL is knowledge you already hold. You learn an enemy weapon exists when it fires at you, so enemy ACTUAL is the only part you can perceive. The overmatch exception is still perception-gated -- you have to have SEEN the auto-cannon; an unseen one contributes nothing to anybody's morale and simply kills someone, which is then the first thing the side learns.

THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MUST BE GOT RIGHT EARLY: MORALE IS A PERCEPTION QUANTITY, NOT A WORLD QUANTITY. It cannot be computed from the true board without cheating. It belongs on the same seam as sightings, computed per side from DemoWorld's _memory[side]. Cheap today, expensive once anything reads it. It also means the same squad legitimately shows a different morale through each viewpoint -- which the viewer can now display rather than hide, since the panel went under fog on 2026-09-04 (b1bdfab).

THREE THINGS THAT MUST LAND FIRST, and none of them is the morale code.

  1. THE RANK LADDER IS TOO SHORT. DemoWorld's rankAt defaults to [50.0, 150.0] -- two thresholds, three ranks, and the code's own comment says that is "roughly one kill and then three". Self-heal gates on IsFullRank, the top of three. Westwood's C&C Generals has FOUR levels (Rookie, Veteran, Elite, Heroic) and self-repair only at Heroic, a much longer climb. Lori: "note how expensive Westwood makes that doctrine: four ranks, only the top one heals at all." So we hand out the ability that changes the whole retreat doctrine at roughly half the price of the model we are copying, and the parked item "Veterans self-heal at full rank, so they stop needing repair pads" is NOT a heal-rate problem -- the ladder is too short, so the top of it is ordinary rather than exceptional. The fix is data: rankAt is a constructor parameter, and IsFullRank reads _rankAt.Length, so a fourth threshold moves the heal gate on its own. One coupling to fix by hand: RetreatByRank is [0.4, 0.55, 0.7], three entries against three ranks, and a fourth needs a real decision rather than an interpolation.

  2. RANK MUST BUY DAMAGE, AND TODAY IT BUYS NOTHING OF THE KIND. Checked every use of RankOf: it scales the kill bonus by the VICTIM's rank, gates self-heal, sets the withdrawal threshold, and feeds the display. Nothing multiplies a unit's output. So a veteran and a rookie contribute identical firepower and the morale bonus would cost the same when either leaves -- the property Lori wants has nothing to couple to. Westwood veterancy raises damage AND rate of fire AND armour; we took the ladder and the self-heal and left the damage bonus behind. That is also why "in earning rank they do more damage and they take more damage" reads as obviously true of the MODEL and is not true of the CODE.

  3. OVERMATCH IS ARMOUR-VERSUS-WARHEAD, NOT RAW DPS. 50 DPS against infantry armour and against vehicle armour are different numbers, so "can this kill me inside one exchange" cannot be asked until the damage matrix exists. The parked item "Combat model: armour type vs weapon type, and blast radius" already carries the shape -- a percentage row per warhead indexed by armour, blast halving per step -- and is now a DEPENDENCY rather than a nice-to-have. It is also where the combat model stops being bookkeeping and becomes doctrine: the reason to know a tank hard-counters your infantry is so your infantry can decline the fight.

WHAT FALLS OUT FOR FREE ONCE IT EXISTS.

  RETREAT AND DEATH BECOME THE SAME EVENT TO THE NEIGHBOURS -- both remove the DPS from local range. That prices a withdrawal policy which is currently free, and it answers the Company of Heroes problem directly (see the research below): CoH's price control for retreat is that the route home is unsafe, and Relic has declined for a decade to make it safe. Here the price is structural instead of being a pathing accident.

  THE CASCADE, WITHOUT SCRIPTING IT. Total War has no group retreat order; a routing unit applies an area morale penalty to its neighbours and a line breaks in a cascade. Ours falls out of the DPS term with no penalty table at all. It is also the first real use for the dead-squad record: a squad emits something to its neighbours as it dies.

  BAIT AS A CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN AN AUTHORED BEHAVIOUR. To break a line you kill or draw off its heaviest hitter first, because that is what drops everyone's morale. The mechanism PRODUCES "apply pressure, then bait" instead of us hand-writing baitability. See [[Doctrine as a weight vector, and temperature as the mechanism for being baited]] -- morale and temperature are the same scalar read two ways: cross the threshold and you disengage, short of it you merely decide worse.

  RETREAT DISTANCE VARIES BY RANK, which decides a parked item. A rookie has no self-heal, so its withdrawal is a long errand to a pad -- expensive, hence held to 0.4. A veteran self-heals, so it needs only to leave the line of fire -- cheap, hence pulled at 0.7. Lori: "A unit that can heal will take even more damage and not bother to back off more than out of the LOF." The parked item "Disengage is a separate primitive from repair" proposes splitting the one retreat verb into step-out-and-hold versus errand-to-a-pad; this says WHICH RANK USES WHICH, which is the part the item was missing.

  AND THE CURRENT CODE IS THE DEGENERATE CASE. RepairPolicy fires on HealthOf(id) < RetreatBelowFor(RankOf(id)), which IS a morale threshold with the bonus term at zero. So this is additive rather than a rewrite, and the existing test corpus is the regression guard: with the bonus at zero every current behaviour must be unchanged.

RANK IS ONE AXIS, NOT TWO, AND THE MODEL IS WESTWOOD'S. I proposed splitting rank into experience and command, on the grounds that senior officers stand at the rear. Lori: "Look at the entire Westwood output, it uses rank the same way - that's been my model." So rank is veterancy: kills earn chevrons, chevrons buy stats, and the reason to pull a veteran early is SCARCITY rather than command -- it is expensive in the only currency that matters, time under fire. Keep the wires separate even so: RetreatByRank is a commander's withdrawal POLICY, and morale is what the unit itself feels. Who you pull out first and who breaks first are different questions, or the table ends up asserting that the best troops are the most cowardly.

I ALSO CALLED TWO PARKED ITEMS CONTRADICTORY AND THEY ARE NOT. "RetreatByRank pulls the veteran out earliest" and "A veteran shields the rookies beside it" are a SEQUENCE, not a tension: the veteran is in front because it does more damage, takes more damage because it is in front, and is pulled early because what is being protected is expensive. Lori: "These two items aren't in as much tension as you think."

TWO FAILURE MODES TO DESIGN AGAINST, both named in shipped games.
  DEATH SPIRAL: loss lowers morale lowers morale. Steel Division 2 shipped panic so cheap that one mortar with zero casualties paralyses an army. The actual-DPS rule is what defends against it here -- a mortar landing nothing does nothing, so PANIC HAS TO BE PAID FOR IN DAMAGE.
  BLOBBING: if morale rewards local firepower density, the doctrine's answer to everything is "stand closer", which fights formations and chokepoints. Company of Heroes' Forward Retreat Points were widely blamed for exactly this.

OPEN, AND NOT ANSWERED HERE. Whether the enemy term subtracts at all or morale is friendly-only. What the local RANGE is, and whether it is the same octile measure as reach, exposure and the leash. Whether morale is per agent or per squad. What the fourth rank's withdrawal threshold should be. And how "out of the line of fire" is expressed at all, given RadiusSight is octile distance whose own comment says walls do not exist, and there is no LOS or Bresenham anywhere in the solution -- so today it can only mean OUT OF RANGE, a circle rather than a shadow.

THE GENERALISATION LORI DREW AT THE END: "A lot of what we want is filters on data streams." True of every item above, and of fog, the panel, narration, the leash and advertisement scoring. The gap it exposes is that GAMEHUB HAS EVENTS AND NO STREAM -- DemoWorld.Fallen is cleared at the head of the next Settle, so a death exists for exactly one tick and only if something reads it that frame, and Entered is the same shape. Every consumer is really doing "read the state before it is overwritten", which is why each new consumer costs a change rather than a subscription. With one append-only per-tick stream, narration is a filter, the dead-squad record is the stream not being discarded, morale is a fold over a window, and the trace file is the stream serialised. The hard part is retention, which is the same question as fog forgetting -- and the research says nobody solves it cleanly: Command: Modern Operations keeps belief until observation contradicts it and STILL expires mobile contacts on a timer. See [[broadcast-not-seams]] and [[design-for-threads]].

RESEARCH BEHIND THE CLAIMS ABOVE: three reports written 2026-09-04, in docs/research/ -- research-retreat.md, research-scale.md, research-fog.md. Published design commentary only; no game source was read, and one source repository that surfaced in results was skipped unopened. See [[clean-room-no-competitor-source]].

heading: Fog is a subscription, not a mask: one rule at three refresh rates
body:
Lori, 2026-09-04, on the later Westwood fog model. BANKED, NOT BUILT. It sits here rather than in the viewer thread because it is a WORLD model rather than a rendering one, and because [[Morale is health plus the guns beside you, minus the guns hitting you]] depends on it -- morale is computed from what a side knows, so what a side knows has to be defined first.

LORI'S DESCRIPTION, which is the whole design: "Your knowledge of the map stayed the same. You know what the terrain looks like. You know what the buildings looked like the last time you were there. You might even know where units were last seen. But you were no longer updated on that information." And then the line that unifies it: "That's why fog for terrain is removed one time."

FOG IS A SUBSCRIPTION, NOT A MASK. While a unit can see a place, the side is subscribed to updates about it. When nobody can see it, the subscription lapses and the last value received simply stands. Nothing is erased and nothing refreshes. This is Lori's own "a lot of what we want is filters on data streams" applied to perception, and it is a different thing from what we have: our fog is a mask over CURRENT truth, plus a separate list of sightings.

IT DISSOLVES THE RETENTION PROBLEM, which I had called the hard part. I was picturing belief as a growing log needing an expiry policy -- which is why Command: Modern Operations ends up with a two-hour timer on mobile contacts even though it corrects belief by observation. Last-value-per-place is not a log. It is O(MAP), NOT O(HISTORY): one slot per cell, overwritten while subscribed, untouched otherwise, bounded by the terrain forever with no policy at all. That is presumably why it shipped.

AND IT GIVES THE BANKED "FORGETS ONLY BY LOOKING" IDEA FOR FREE. There is no forgetting mechanism because nothing forgets -- it OVERWRITES. Look at a place and find nothing and the update writes "nothing here". Belief corrected by observation, with no timer, no decay and no area of uncertainty.

ONE RULE AT THREE REFRESH RATES, which is the part that makes it elegant. The research could find no designer statement anywhere explaining why RTS games remember buildings forever and forget units instantly. Under this model there is nothing to explain, because it is not an asymmetry:
  TERRAIN    never changes    -- last value is permanently correct, so lift the fog ONCE and never re-subscribe
  BUILDINGS  changes rarely   -- last value usually right, occasionally rubble
  UNITS      changes per tick -- last value wrong almost immediately
Nobody wrote a rule about buildings. They wrote "keep the last thing you saw", and the three behaviours fall out of how fast the underlying thing moves. The dev-blog rationalisations the research did find -- statics are strategic knowledge, mobiles are tactical uncertainty -- describe the consequence and call it the cause.

THE ONE GENUINE DESIGN CHOICE ON TOP OF THE MECHANISM: most RTS SUPPRESS the stale unit marker rather than drawing it. That is an override, not a consequence, and it is where the research's sharpest line bites -- Wayward Strategy, that in an RTS "information revealed by an enemy unit is always actionable by a player's other units". A stale building is information; a stale unit position is a TARGET, and a wrong one.

WE DRAW GHOSTS, so we have already departed from that convention, and the departure is defensible for a reason specific to this project: OURS ARE FOR THE WATCHER, NOT FOR THE DOCTRINE. The doctrine reads _memory[side]; the ghost is a rendering of it. If those two ever became the same surface we would have shipped exactly the mistake every RTS avoids. As long as the ghost draws what the doctrine believes, it is an instrument reading -- and the fact that it can be CONFIDENTLY WRONG is the point rather than a defect. A doctrine acting on a building that is rubble, or a squad that left twenty ticks ago, with no way to know until it looks, is the behaviour the viewpoint cycle exists to catch.

WHERE OURS DIFFERS TODAY, precisely. DemoWorld banks sightings per SIDE in _memory[side] -- which is already the right home, and is why what a squad saw outlives the squad. But a sighting is an EVENT CARRYING A TICK, and the viewer fades it by age (ViewerApp.GhostFade = 120 ticks). That constant is written as a display constant and explicitly not a doctrine's forgetting time, so nothing expires in the doctrine today. The divergence is in SHAPE rather than in behaviour: we hold a fading list of timestamped events where Westwood holds a frozen map. The two read the same while only the renderer consumes them, and diverge the moment anything REASONS over them -- which is exactly what the morale model would do.

RELATED AND UNRESOLVED: the retention question is the same question as the events-without-a-stream gap recorded in the morale entry. A last-value-per-place store is the bounded answer for PERCEPTION; it is not an answer for the event log narration wants, where the history is the point. Two different structures, and conflating them is the trap.
